retained_finding: DBOS is a strong source donor for the WP105 retry-identity blocker, but the evidence supports pattern distillation rather than runtime import. Current DBOS source validates durable workflow IDs, reuses recorded completed outcomes instead of re-running the body, and aborts duplicate ownership conflicts. Its historical issue #759 shows why identity admission must fail closed: malformed durable identity once caused repeated duplicate side effects before the fix. The full runtime would add a second durable workflow/control authority and a larger dependency surface, so F2 should instead transplant the tested invariants into existing UnifiedDB/EffectJournal.
hypothesis_forwarded: Persist operation_retry_id + operation_payload_sha256 + attempt_id + dispatch-start state + outcome certainty + verification reference transactionally inside the existing EffectJournal/UnifiedDB lane; keep request_sha256 and effect_id distinct. Same logical operation and payload must fence or return the existing record; changed payload under the same operation ID must reject before dispatch; unresolved UNKNOWN non-idempotent outcomes must never auto-replay.
counterhypothesis: Identity plus payload digest may still be insufficient without an explicit authority-owned PRE_DISPATCH/DISPATCH_STARTED_UNKNOWN/VERIFIED terminal state machine; the next no-real-effect reopen fixture must falsify this.
next_gate: Acquire a separate E2 architecture-mapping claim and map the pattern against exact current WP105/EffectJournal schema before any build handoff or runtime test.
authority_fence: Provenance mirror only. F2 claim/result and pending_research.sqlite retain Trigger-6 authority roles; UnifiedDB and EffectGate/EffectJournal remain canonical state/effect authority.
